title: Transit: channel closure as ingestion shutdown signal
description: Transit shutdown drops ingestion_sender (the last Arc clone of the mpsc Sender) immediately after the select\! loop exits, which causes the ingestion task's 'while let Some(article) = ingestion_receiver.recv().await' to return None once the queue is empty and then stop naturally. This is the idiomatic Rust/tokio channel pattern: the channel itself becomes the shutdown signal, so no separate stop flag, broadcast channel, or CancellationToken is needed. The ingestion task drains all queued articles before exiting, ensuring no in-flight work is lost. Alternative rejected: a separate AtomicBool shutdown flag checked inside the recv loop. That would require the task to poll or be interrupted mid-item and adds a synchronization primitive that the channel already subsumes.
